\section{Experimental Results}
\label{sec:results}

Results use the fixed 4,218/1,406/1,406 design split and seed 128 described in
Section~\ref{sec:methodology}. The test designs were held out from fitting, but
their results had been inspected during model development; the comparisons are
therefore retrospective rather than untouched confirmation.

Table~\ref{tab:common-s7-results} shows that the frequency-dependent mean curve
was a stronger reference than the global mean: Scalar Ridge did not improve on
it. Increasing generic point-wise capacity also did not consistently reduce
test error in the selected configurations; the complete comparison is retained
in Appendix E. Curve Neural gave the lowest
$IL_{7,1}$ MAE. Relative to Polynomial MLP, its paired design-level change was
$-0.1204$~dB (95\% bootstrap interval $[-0.1613,-0.0774]$~dB). The interval
excludes zero but crosses the project-defined $-0.10$~dB interpretation boundary.

On the complete complex task, the neural model improved both metrics over the
training-mean matrix (Table~\ref{tab:full-matrix-results}) and reproduced
design-dependent reflection and crosstalk structure in
Fig.~\ref{fig:page4-response-evidence}. Its extracted $IL_{7,1}$ error was,
however, higher than Curve Neural by $+3.4020$~dB (95\% interval
$[+3.3104,+3.4901]$~dB); the models also differ in architecture, targets,
scaling and loss.

Reciprocal reconstruction gave a zero test-prediction reciprocity residual.
None of the 281,200 test design--frequency matrices violated the sampled
passivity condition; the largest predicted singular value was 0.9141. The
finite-band causality residual was 0.4812 for prediction versus 0.3173 for the
simulated test response. These are diagnostics, not evidence that passivity or
causality was enforced or guaranteed. Both bootstrap intervals resample the
1,406 test designs conditional on fixed selected models; they omit training-seed,
model-search and prior test-exposure uncertainty.
